payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery chemistry designed to reduce electrolyte crossover and aging. An independent Halvorsen-Pike Laboratories audit corrected the initial cycle-life claim: the governing result is 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold, replacing the retracted 12,000-cycle figure. The prototype achieved a gravimetric energy density of 148 Wh/kg. At 500 MWh manufacturing scale, projected stack-level cost is $61/kWh. The chemistry has an operating-temperature floor of 4 °C because the dopant precipitates below that temperature, requiring cycling to stop.
